content:
# ACK S3 Logs Bucket and IAM Policy Grant

I'll add a new logs bucket to both environments with versioning, encryption, and public access blocking, plus grant the existing service principals GetObject/PutObject access to the logs bucket only.

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-dev
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/iam.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: User
metadata:
  name: myapp-user-dev
spec:
  userName: myapp-user-dev
  inlinePolicies:
    # Keep existing assets policy unchanged
    myapp-assets-policy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject",
              "s3:ListBucket"
            ],
            "Resource": [
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-dev",
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-dev/*"
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    # Grant logs bucket access
    myapp-logs-policy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
          }
        ]
      }
```

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-prod
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/iam.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-role-prod
spec:
  roleName: myapp-role-prod
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Principal": {
            "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/OIDC_ID"
          },
          "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
          "Condition": {
            "StringEquals": {
              "oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/OIDC_ID:sub": "system:serviceaccount:default:myapp"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  inlinePolicies:
    # Keep existing assets policy unchanged
    myapp-assets-policy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject",
              "s3:ListBucket"
            ],
            "Resource": [
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-prod",
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-prod/*"
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    # Grant logs bucket access
    myapp-logs-policy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
          }
        ]
      }
```

**Summary:**
- **Buckets**: New ACK `Bucket` resources with versioning, AES-256 encryption, and all public access flags blocked
- **Dev IAM**: Added `myapp-logs-policy` inline policy to existing User, granting GetObject/PutObject on logs bucket only
- **Prod IAM**: Added `myapp-logs-policy` inline policy to existing Role, same permissions scoped to prod logs bucket
- **Independence**: Each environment's bucket and policy are fully isolated; dev changes do not affect prod

Apply with:
```bash
kubectl apply -f dev/
kubectl apply -f prod/
```
